title: 🚁 Driverless flying taxi carries a passenger in Japan!
body: 🚁 Driverless flying taxi carries a passenger in Japan!

An electric driverless flying taxi carried a passenger during a public demonstration on Friday, November 20, in Yamanashi Prefecture, Japan — a sight that brings the future of urban air travel one step closer.
The aircraft is the Chinese-made EH216-S, an electric vertical take-off and landing vehicle that seats two passengers and carries no pilot on board, flying autonomously along a pre-programmed route.

In the demonstration, held at the Japan Aviation Academy in the city of Kai, the aircraft flew one passenger 380 metres along the runway in front of visitors and journalists, then made a second, passenger-free flight of 1,800 metres over the nearby Kamanashi River.

The aircraft runs on sixteen propellers and has received type, production and operation certificates in China — the only one in the world so far to hold the full set of these certificates for a passenger drone.

But the road to a commercial service is still long: the demonstration took place in a controlled test environment and does not mean opening ticket bookings for passengers, as licences and regulations for regular passenger services are still being prepared in most countries.

All eyes are on Dubai, where the company aims to launch its first passenger service before the end of 2026, while other companies such as Joby and Archer continue their certification stages in the United States and Europe.
Simply put: a taxi that flies you without a pilot is no longer science fiction — but it is still a trial demonstration before it becomes a means of transport you buy a ticket for.
Would you ride a driverless flying taxi if you had the chance?
